pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Scale and diversification support the profile, but earnings quality is flattered. Fuel distribution, pipelines, terminals and the refinery all contribute, with fuel distribution about half of segment Adjusted EBITDA, yet trailing reported EBITDA of USD 3,624 million holds net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million and adjusted EBITDA holds a one-time first-quarter gain of USD 102 million; removing that gain lifts net leverage from 3.51x to 3.61x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02

Leverage is moderate and falling, but the fall is earnings-driven rather than repayment-driven. Net debt moved by only USD 95 million from year-end 2025 while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 1,488 million, and free cash flow after distributions was USD 856 million over the trailing year, 6.90% of net debt, so lower leverage depends on holding the acquired earnings. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05

Liquidity covers the nearest maturities with room to spare. Cash and unused revolver of USD 3,060 million are 1.57x the USD 1,949 million of notes due in 2027 and 2028, the revolver runs to June 2030, and the largest maturity is USD 2,723 million in 2029. The 2027 notes are classified as long-term only because management intends to refinance them, and availability after the Offen purchase is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15

Acquisitions and distributions are the main policy risks. The Offen purchase raises net debt to USD 13,003 million, 3.59x calculated reported EBITDA, before any Offen earnings, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth leans on external funding; governance risk is medium because a controlling owner holds broad discretion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09

The structure ranks the secured revolver ahead of equal-ranking unsecured notes, and note holders depend on subsidiaries outside the guarantee. Senior unsecured notes are 92.22% of principal and the secured revolver 0.84%, while non-guarantor subsidiaries earned 46.77% of nine-month net income and the guarantor group's liabilities exceed its assets before investments in them. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

runs.text: Strengths. The first strength is earnings scale across four segments: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,889 million came 53.86% from fuel distribution, 18.52% from pipelines, 11.84% from terminals and 15.78% from the refinery, so no single segment decides debt service, which lowers the odds that one shock breaks leverage. The second is liquidity of USD 3,060 million, 23.25% of total debt, with no note maturing in 2026 and a revolver to 2030, which gives time to refinance the 2027 notes. The third is equity-like funding of the largest deal, with Class D units of USD 2,547 million and preferred units of USD 1.47 billion, which limited the debt added and supports the 3.5x covenant leverage. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 22

Weaknesses. The first weakness is dependence on acquired and inventory-driven earnings: the trailing figures hold net inventory gains of USD 258 million and a one-time gain of USD 102 million, so the ratio can rise quickly if margins revert. The second is policy risk from the controller: distributions of USD 880 million in nine months, a distribution growth aim of at least 5%, incentive distribution rights taking 28.46% of the third-quarter payout and the Offen purchase after the quarter. The third is structure: note holders depend on subsidiaries that earned 46.77% of net income but do not guarantee, and the rank of the GoZone Bonds and lease-related debt is not stated. The fourth is a lumpy maturity profile with USD 2,723 million due in 2029 and USD 1,949 million in 2027 and 2028. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C07

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The defining transaction is the Parkland acquisition, which closed on 2025-10-31: Sunoco paid Parkland shareholders cash and issued Class D units to SunocoCorp, whose units were exchanged for Parkland shares, and it assumed or exchanged about USD 3.65 billion of Parkland debt into its own notes. The financing before closing was USD 1.0 billion of 5.625% notes due 2031 and USD 900 million of 5.875% notes due 2034 in September 2025, alongside 1.5 million 7.875% Series A preferred units with net proceeds of about USD 1.47 billion. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8, 89, 237, 249; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

After Parkland the group completed TanQuid on 2026-01-16, with equity consideration of EUR 206 million and assumed debt of EUR 298 million, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about USD 81 million, funded from cash and the Credit Facility. In March 2026 it issued USD 600 million of 5.375% notes due 2031 and USD 600 million of 5.625% notes due 2034 and used part of the proceeds to redeem USD 500 million of 2026 notes and USD 600 million of 2027 notes, then redeemed the remaining Parkland notes and, by August 2026, its Canadian-dollar notes. The Offen Petroleum acquisition, closed on 2026-10-27 for approximately USD 600 million in cash, is after the quarter end and not in any reported balance. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 10, 14; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_ex991sunerq12026.htm.jsonl, page 2

The registrant also converted from a Delaware to a Texas limited partnership, with the Plan of Conversion dated 2026-07-02, and moved its listing to the Texas Stock Exchange; the related current report and the new partnership agreement are not in the documents supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_sun-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 51

fields.value: Financial foundation for Sunoco LP (issuer id sun) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is Sunoco LP consolidated statements for FY2024, FY2025, nine months and the third quarter of 2026 against 2025, carrying-value debt, liquidity, the maturity ladder, derived trailing figures and the events after September 30, 2026 that the sources state.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sunoco LP's net debt was USD 12,403 million at September 30, 2026, or 3.51x trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves creditors with moderate leverage and ample interest cover, but the roughly USD 600 million Offen purchase that closed after the quarter already raises it.

fields.value: Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 760 million of cash plus USD 2,300 million of unused revolver, or USD 3,060 million, which is 23.25% of total debt. The revolver matures in June 2030, and USD 1,049 million of 2027 notes are classified as long-term only because management intends to refinance them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Senior unsecured notes make up USD 12,213 million of USD 13,243 million of principal, so the drawn revolver of USD 111 million is the only debt stated as secured, and the structure leans on subsidiary guarantees and equal-ranking unsecured claims. Maturities run USD 1,049 million in 2027, USD 900 million in 2028 and USD 2,723 million in 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two events after the quarter are stated but not in any period figure: the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million, closed on 2026-10-27, and the third-quarter distribution of USD 267 million payable on 2026-11-19. Net debt alone after each would be USD 13,003 million (3.59x reported EBITDA) and USD 12,670 million (3.50x). How Offen was funded and what it earns are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that trailing issuer-adjusted EBITDA still holds a one-time first-quarter inventory gain of USD 102 million; without it net debt to adjusted EBITDA is 3.61x rather than 3.51x. Trailing reported EBITDA is flattered by net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million, and the refinery segment contributed USD 238 million of adjusted EBITDA in the third quarter against USD 456 million across nine months, a pace that the first-quarter turnaround makes hard to extrapolate. The view would weaken if the Offen purchase was debt funded and earns little in its first year, or if inventory and refinery margins normalise; it would strengthen if the next quarterly report shows leverage near the current level after Offen is included.

fields.value: Business & governance for Sunoco LP (issuer id sun) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sunoco LP's creditors face medium governance and structure risk: an Energy Transfer-controlled general partner holds broad discretion over borrowing, distributions and acquisitions, while the notes are guaranteed by only part of a group that earns nearly half its profit outside the guarantor perimeter.

fields.value: The business itself is diversified and fee-supported: fuel distribution earned about 53.86% of nine-month 2026 segment Adjusted EBITDA, with pipelines, terminals and the acquired refinery supplying the rest. Distributions have risen eight quarters in a row and the third-quarter payout was covered 2.20x by adjusted distributable cash flow, and recent acquisitions were funded partly with preferred and Class D units rather than debt alone, which tempers the risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Energy Transfer controls the borrower through its general partner, and the partnership agreement lets that general partner weigh Energy Transfer's interests against those of the partnership and its unitholders. Energy Transfer owns all of the general partner, 20.79% of the common units and every incentive distribution right, and its power to appoint the board runs through SunocoCorp under a delegation agreement. Five of the seven directors were independent at year-end 2025 and an independent audit committee oversees reporting, but the annual report describes no creditor vote, and the general partner alone decides borrowing, reserves, asset sales and whether spending counts as maintenance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Related-party dealings are large in volume but small against cost of sales, and they rose sharply in 2026. Purchases of motor fuel from Energy Transfer affiliates were USD 1,249 million in FY2025, 5.57% of cost of sales, and USD 1,760 million in nine months 2026, 4.60% of cost of sales, while sales to affiliates reached USD 884 million against USD 15 million a year earlier. Reimbursements to the general partner were USD 43 million in FY2025 with no cap in the partnership agreement, so the exposure is leakage and pricing discipline rather than funding, and the pricing basis is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Distributions take a large and rising share of cash flow, but coverage is ample and growth is deliberate policy. Distributions paid were USD 880 million in nine months 2026, 39.09% of operating cash flow, and the third-quarter distribution per unit is 10.28% above a year earlier, the eighth consecutive increase against management's stated multi-year distribution growth rate of at least 5%. Adjusted distributable cash flow covered the USD 267 million third-quarter payout 2.20x, but incentive distribution rights take 28.46% of it, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth capital and acquisitions rely mainly on external financing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisition appetite is high and recent funding mixed debt with equity-like claims. Since 2024 the group closed the NuStar, Parkland, TanQuid and Delta purchases, and the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million closed after the quarter. Parkland was paid for with cash and Class D units issued to SunocoCorp, the cash raised through USD 1.9 billion of new senior notes and USD 1.47 billion of Series A preferred units, which keeps part of the burden outside debt but adds preferred distributions of about USD 118.1 million a year that rank ahead of common units. Management says leverage returned to its target in less than one year, but the target level is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is diversified but still earns about half its segment profit from motor fuel distribution. In nine months 2026 fuel distribution produced 53.86% of segment Adjusted EBITDA, pipelines 18.52%, terminals 11.84% and the refinery 15.78%, and the refinery's quarterly Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 43 million in the first quarter of 2026, hit by a turnaround, to USD 175 million and then USD 238 million. Contractually committed revenue of USD 2,038 million at September 30, 2026 gives some visibility, and 89.26% of FY2025 revenue was in the United States before a full year of Parkland's Canadian and Caribbean operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors rely on guarantees from only part of the group. In nine months 2026 the guarantor issuer group had USD 22,894 million of revenue and USD 758 million of net income, against USD 20,080 million and USD 667 million for the non-guarantor subsidiaries, whose long-term assets were USD 11,730 million; the notes are structurally subordinated to the non-guarantors' debts. Before USD 5,510 million of investments in non-guarantors, the guarantor group's liabilities exceeded its assets by USD 2,031 million, so note holders depend on the value of those subsidiaries.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Exchange and domicile changes lighten outside governance checks. Sunoco converted from a Delaware to a Texas limited partnership under a plan dated 2026-07-02, and its units are now listed on the Texas Stock Exchange, which does not require a majority-independent board or compensation and nominating committees for a partnership; the general partner's own agreement still requires at least three independent directors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a medium risk view is that equity-like funding carried the largest deal. Class D units valued at USD 2,547 million and USD 1.47 billion of preferred units went into Parkland, leverage on the issuer's own covenant basis fell from 4.03x at year-end 2025 to 3.5x at September 30, 2026, distributions are well covered and the board has a majority of independent directors. That would point to low risk if repeated, and it wins if the next acquisitions are equity funded and distribution growth is paced to deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if the Offen purchase was debt funded without deleveraging, if related-party sales keep growing from USD 884 million, or if the delegation agreement or the listing change were used to reduce creditor information or consent rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The defining transaction is the Parkland acquisition, which closed on 2025-10-31: Sunoco paid Parkland shareholders cash and issued Class D units to SunocoCorp, whose units were exchanged for Parkland shares, and it assumed or exchanged about USD 3.65 billion of Parkland debt into its own notes. The financing before closing was USD 1.0 billion of 5.625% notes due 2031 and USD 900 million of 5.875% notes due 2034 in September 2025, alongside 1.5 million 7.875% Series A preferred units with net proceeds of about USD 1.47 billion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: After Parkland the group completed TanQuid on 2026-01-16, with equity consideration of EUR 206 million and assumed debt of EUR 298 million, and Delta on 2026-04-01 for about USD 81 million, funded from cash and the Credit Facility. In March 2026 it issued USD 600 million of 5.375% notes due 2031 and USD 600 million of 5.625% notes due 2034 and used part of the proceeds to redeem USD 500 million of 2026 notes and USD 600 million of 2027 notes, then redeemed the remaining Parkland notes and, by August 2026, its Canadian-dollar notes. The Offen Petroleum acquisition, closed on 2026-10-27 for approximately USD 600 million in cash, is after the quarter end and not in any reported balance.

fields.value: The registrant also converted from a Delaware to a Texas limited partnership, with the Plan of Conversion dated 2026-07-02, and moved its listing to the Texas Stock Exchange; the related current report and the new partnership agreement are not in the documents supplied.

fields.value: Fundamental credit for Sunoco LP (issuer id sun) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is an integrated view of business risk, financial profile, liquidity, structure, governance, outlook and the primary downside path, built on the financial foundation and the business and governance analysis for the same date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sunoco LP is an adequate, moderately leveraged credit: liquidity of USD 3,060 million and a diversified earnings base support it, while leverage that rests on acquired earnings and a controlling owner's discretion limits headroom.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt was USD 12,403 million at September 30, 2026, 3.51x trailing adjusted EBITDA, and USD 13,003 million pro forma for the Offen purchase of approximately USD 600 million that closed on 2026-10-27; cash interest is covered 4.87x. Distributions absorb much of free cash flow, so leverage falls only if earnings hold. The primary downside path is a fall in fuel margins to the 2025 level, which would lift leverage to 4.18x without threatening liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and diversification support the profile, but earnings quality is flattered. Fuel distribution, pipelines, terminals and the refinery all contribute, with fuel distribution about half of segment Adjusted EBITDA, yet trailing reported EBITDA of USD 3,624 million holds net inventory valuation gains of USD 258 million and adjusted EBITDA holds a one-time first-quarter gain of USD 102 million; removing that gain lifts net leverage from 3.51x to 3.61x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C02

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is moderate and falling, but the fall is earnings-driven rather than repayment-driven. Net debt moved by only USD 95 million from year-end 2025 while trailing adjusted EBITDA rose by USD 1,488 million, and free cash flow after distributions was USD 856 million over the trailing year, 6.90% of net debt, so lower leverage depends on holding the acquired earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity covers the nearest maturities with room to spare. Cash and unused revolver of USD 3,060 million are 1.57x the USD 1,949 million of notes due in 2027 and 2028, the revolver runs to June 2030, and the largest maturity is USD 2,723 million in 2029. The 2027 notes are classified as long-term only because management intends to refinance them, and availability after the Offen purchase is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and distributions are the main policy risks. The Offen purchase raises net debt to USD 13,003 million, 3.59x calculated reported EBITDA, before any Offen earnings, and the partnership agreement requires distribution of available cash, so growth leans on external funding; governance risk is medium because a controlling owner holds broad discretion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C09

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The structure ranks the secured revolver ahead of equal-ranking unsecured notes, and note holders depend on subsidiaries outside the guarantee. Senior unsecured notes are 92.22% of principal and the secured revolver 0.84%, while non-guarantor subsidiaries earned 46.77% of nine-month net income and the guarantor group's liabilities exceed its assets before investments in them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is that leverage on the issuer's own covenant basis fell from 4.03x at year-end 2025 to 3.5x at September 30, 2026, management expects 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to exceed its raised guidance range of USD 3.5 billion to USD 3.7 billion, and Parkland was funded partly with equity-like units. If the next quarter shows leverage at or below the current level after Offen, with distributions held within coverage, the view would move toward strong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a weaker credit is that the improvement rests on one year of acquired earnings and inventory gains. If fuel margins revert to the 2025 level while Offen is debt funded, leverage reaches 4.39x on the calculated basis, and the view would weaken if distributions continue to grow faster than cash retained for repayment.

fields.value: - No sector data or peer set was supplied, so the business profile is not compared with typical leveraged issuers and the competitive-advantage judgement rests on the issuer's own descriptions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. The first strength is earnings scale across four segments: nine-month 2026 Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,889 million came 53.86% from fuel distribution, 18.52% from pipelines, 11.84% from terminals and 15.78% from the refinery, so no single segment decides debt service, which lowers the odds that one shock breaks leverage. The second is liquidity of USD 3,060 million, 23.25% of total debt, with no note maturing in 2026 and a revolver to 2030, which gives time to refinance the 2027 notes. The third is equity-like funding of the largest deal, with Class D units of USD 2,547 million and preferred units of USD 1.47 billion, which limited the debt added and supports the 3.5x covenant leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 15, 22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. The first weakness is dependence on acquired and inventory-driven earnings: the trailing figures hold net inventory gains of USD 258 million and a one-time gain of USD 102 million, so the ratio can rise quickly if margins revert. The second is policy risk from the controller: distributions of USD 880 million in nine months, a distribution growth aim of at least 5%, incentive distribution rights taking 28.46% of the third-quarter payout and the Offen purchase after the quarter. The third is structure: note holders depend on subsidiaries that earned 46.77% of net income but do not guarantee, and the rank of the GoZone Bonds and lease-related debt is not stated. The fourth is a lumpy maturity profile with USD 2,723 million due in 2029 and USD 1,949 million in 2027 and 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C07

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sunoco LP distributes motor fuel to about 11,000 branded and partner locations, owns about 14,000 miles of pipeline, over 170 terminals and a refinery in British Columbia, and operates in 33 countries and territories. Contract-based dealer and commission-agent supply, fee-based pipelines and terminals and a regulated tariff base give cash-flow visibility, but most revenue is fuel sold at pass-through prices, so earnings follow the margin per gallon, not revenue. The group grew by acquisition (NuStar in 2024, Parkland in 2025, then TanQuid, Delta and Offen), which adds scale and integration risk and raises debt service needs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Energy Transfer owns the general partner, 20.8% of the common units and all incentive distribution rights, and appoints the board through SunocoCorp, which holds the Class D units. The general partner may favour its owner, has no cap on cost reimbursements and decides borrowing and distributions, so financial policy is the owner's to set; the independent audit committee and five independent directors out of seven are the checks. Debt is issued at Sunoco LP, Sunoco Finance Corp and NuStar Logistics with reciprocal subsidiary guarantees, and non-guarantor subsidiaries, including Parkland businesses, sit structurally ahead of the notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is mainly fuel sold at market-linked prices: fuel was 95.54% of third-quarter revenue, so the revenue line says little about credit quality and the margin per gallon, 16.9 cents in nine months 2026 against 10.9 cents a year earlier, matters most. Long-term dealer contracts and branded supply agreements give volume visibility, while commodity price swings, a shift to alternative fuels and supplier dependence limit pricing power. Contractually committed revenue is USD 2,038 million at September 30, 2026, small against fuel revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 37; 10-K_2025-12-31_sun-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Costs are mostly pass-through fuel cost, with operating, lease and administrative costs of USD 1,664 million in nine months 2026 against USD 644 million a year earlier after Parkland. Margin resilience therefore depends on gross profit per gallon and on volume, not on cutting costs, and the first-quarter inventory gain and net inventory valuation gains show how timing effects move reported earnings. The group can defend margins in a volume dip through branded supply contracts, but not against a sharp margin compression.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow was USD 1,905 million over the trailing year after capital expenditure of USD 738 million, and about USD 1,049 million of distributions leave USD 856 million before acquisitions. Maintenance capital spending of USD 400 million to USD 450 million and growth capital of at least USD 600 million are planned for 2026, so growth spending is the flexible lever if liquidity tightens. Cash interest of USD 726 million takes 20.54% of trailing adjusted EBITDA, and operating cash flow benefited from a USD 316 million working-capital release in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C03; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense and margins are narrow in wholesale and retail fuel, so a competitor price move quickly compresses the per-gallon margin. New entrants face high asset costs in pipelines and terminals, while retail fuel already faces many competitors across store formats, which caps pricing in that part of the portfolio. Substitutes, mainly alternative fuels and efficiency gains, are a long-dated volume risk the annual report flags. Buyers have contract-bound volumes through dealers, which limits switching, and suppliers, with Chevron, Exxon, Phillips 66 and Valero the largest branded sources, hold bargaining power over supply and trade credit terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulation and litigation are the material factors. The pipeline tariff index was reset in April 2026 to producer prices minus 0.55% for five years from July 2026, which slows regulated pipeline revenue growth; Sunoco and an affiliate face climate-change lawsuits in several states with no loss estimate; foreign currency exposure produced a loss of USD 94 million in nine months 2026; and variable-rate debt of USD 398 million is exposed to rate moves of about USD 4 million a year per 100 bp. Other political, social and technology factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the documents read.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are the diversified segment base, the liquidity and maturity runway, and equity-like funding of Parkland. Weaknesses are acquisition-driven earnings, inventory-timing gains, the controller's policy discretion and structural subordination. Opportunities are integration benefits, with management expecting 2026 Adjusted EBITDA above its range, and refinancing the 2027 notes at longer maturity. Threats are margin compression, an Offen purchase that earns little, tariff pressure on pipelines and climate or tax disputes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over twelve to twenty-four months the supportive items are a full year of Parkland, management guidance above its USD 3.5 billion to USD 3.7 billion range and planned growth spending that can be trimmed; the pressures are the Offen purchase, 2027 and 2028 refinancing of USD 1,949 million and inventory timing that reverses. Over three to five years the pipeline tariff index, fuel demand and the integration of a larger Canadian and Caribbean footprint decide whether leverage settles near the current level. The documents do not state a leverage target, so the direction of deleveraging is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C02; EX-99.1_2026-11-03_ex991sunocoandsunococorper.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-04_ex991sunerq22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_sun-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 30

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A realistic downside starts with the fuel margin falling from 16.9 cents per gallon in nine months 2026 to the 13.2 cents of FY2025, a drop of 3.7 cents. On trailing volume of 15,432 million gallons, each cent per gallon is worth about USD 154.3 million of EBITDA, so the drop removes USD 571 million, 16.15% of adjusted EBITDA. Trailing adjusted EBITDA falls to USD 2,964 million, net debt to EBITDA rises from 3.51x to 4.18x, or 4.39x if the Offen purchase is added without earnings, and cash interest cover falls to 4.08x. Free cash flow falls to about USD 1,334 million before tax effects, still above distributions of USD 1,049 million, so liquidity of USD 3,060 million covers the 2027 and 2028 notes without distress, but deleveraging stalls and management's levers are growth spending and the pace of distributions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Sunoco LP presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, segment diversification and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by earnings that rely on acquisitions and inventory timing, a controlling owner's policy discretion and structural subordination. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because free cash flow covers distributions, though not with a wide margin. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on holding leverage near 3.51x through the Offen integration and on market access for the 2027 notes. The primary downside path is margin compression with a debt-funded acquisition, and further analysis would need a rating, the credit agreement and Offen's earnings. Top risk: margin compression while distributions and acquisition funding continue.
